title: the-wiring-links-missing-verbs-not-only-missing-directories
author: cc
what: The instance wiring links every class-space verb that has no instance link yet, instead of only wiring devices whose instance bin does not exist at all -- and it wires the instance a spawn just created, not only instance 0.
why: Today 'a new verb is reachable' is enforced by whoever remembers to delete an instance bin directory or make a symlink by hand. That is policy where it should be physics (Law 4), and it bites immediately: ~/.cairn/devices/cairn/0/bin holds one hand-placed file, so the wiring skips the cairn device forever and `cairn restart` would land in a class bin nothing ever links. The same missing precision leaves `cairn cc restart spawn N` standing up a tmux session and a flags home for instance N with no ~/.cairn/devices/cc/N/bin behind them.
how: launchers/bootstrap.sh already holds both halves. `_cairn_wire_device` mkdirs the instance bin and symlinks every executable in the class bin, but returns early when the instance bin DIRECTORY exists. `_cairn_wire_single`, ten lines away, already has the per-FILE rule: skip when that name exists, link when it does not. Move the skip from the directory into the per-script loop, keep every ln non-fatal, and keep the walk idempotent -- it runs on every bin/cairn floor check. The second half is the instance argument: `_cairn_wire_device` already takes one and only the discovery loop's constant 0 stops it being used, so cmd_spawn in cairn/devices/cc/0/bin/restart calls the wiring for the instance it just chose.
traces_to: Law 4 -- a rule that matters is enforced by physics, not policy. Also Law 1: the recipe was compiled once (ticket 0853294fe972 lifted it whole so it would have one address and no copy); a verb that silently fails to appear makes the next mind re-derive why.
falsifier: GREEN when a verb added to an already-wired device's class bin is reachable as `cairn <device> <verb>` after the wiring runs, with no hand symlink and no directory deleted; and when `cairn cc restart spawn N` leaves ~/.cairn/devices/cc/N/bin holding the same links instance 0 holds. RED if the walk links anything that is not an executable file in a class bin, or if re-running it churns links that already point correctly.

constraints.text: Nothing here may be fatal. The function's own contract is 'nothing here is fatal -- a link that cannot be made is a finding the first run prints, not an abort', so every ln stays `|| true` and the function still returns 0 against an unwritable instance root.
Idempotent. The walk runs on every bin/cairn floor check, so a second run over a fully wired device must churn nothing.

STALE LINKS ARE NOT PRUNED. This change links what is missing and removes nothing: instance-space has no undo (bin/cmd/deletegate carries the reason), and ~/.cairn/devices/cairn/0/bin/cairn is a hand-placed file a pruner would delete. A dangling link left by a deleted class file stays a known, named gap.
The per-file rule is COPIED, not invented: `_cairn_wire_single` in the same function already implements it for superclaude, whose launcher lives outside a device bin.
The 'wired N skipped M' line's numbers change meaning from devices to files. Say so in the line rather than leaving the number to be misread (Law 7 at a diagnostic surface).

children: none, because the two halves are one defect -- the device walk skips on a DIRECTORY and passes instance 0 always, and both are the same missing precision about what the unit of wiring is. Splitting them would leave `cairn cc.1 restart` resolving to nothing even after ticket 55fc9263bf5a teaches the dispatcher to read the address.
questions: none, because nothing here is a spec choice. The rule being applied already exists in the same function (launchers/bootstrap.sh, `_cairn_wire_single`), the instance parameter already exists on `_cairn_wire_device`, and the one thing that could have been a fork -- whether stale links are pruned as well -- is settled OUT by physics rather than by taste: instance-space has no undo (bin/cmd/deletegate carries the reason).

watchme.trigger: a beat on which some class-space cairn/devices/*/0/bin/<verb> has no corresponding link in that device's instance bin. The probe fires on the heartbeat that already runs -- the comparison is two directory reads, and it is the same comparison the wiring itself makes.
watchme.enough: three consecutive verbs added to already-wired devices that are reachable without a hand, at which point the probe retires. The count is of VERBS ADDED, not of clean beats -- a quiet week proves nothing about a rule that only bites when someone adds a verb.
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against this ticket's falsifier, naming the unlinked verb and its device, so the carry says what was missed rather than that something was.
watchme.nexus: the hypothesize tree -- an unlinked verb surviving a beat kills the hypothesis that running the recipe on every bin/cairn floor check is enough, and points at wiring from the act that adds the verb instead.
watchme.consumer: whoever next types `cairn <device> <verb>` and gets 'no such verb' -- surfaced on the cairn device's pane, because an unreachable verb is a live trouble and not a log line.

links.what: cairn restart cycles the system -- its verb lands in cairn/devices/cairn/0/bin, the class bin this wiring skips forever. That build makes its own link by hand; this ticket is why it should not have had to.
the dispatcher resolves an instance address. That ticket teaches `cairn cc.1 restart` to RESOLVE; this one makes there be something at the other end.
lifted the wiring recipe whole out of bootstrap_first_run.sh so it would have one address and two callers. This ticket fixes the unit of work inside that one address.
cairn_wire_instances -- _cairn_wire_device (the directory early return), _cairn_wire_single (the per-file rule to copy), and the discovery loop that passes 0.
cmd_spawn -- knows the instance number it just chose and today leaves it unwired.

notes.text: Found while building Akien's three restart names. MEASURED: ~/.cairn/devices/cairn/0/bin contains one hand-placed file (a shim-printing script, 338 bytes, placed 2026-09-02), and cairn/devices/cairn/0/bin does not exist in class-space at all -- so the cairn device has never been wired by the recipe and never will be while the directory-level early return stands.
